key_insight: The paper benchmarks four operator-learning deep surrogates for aerodynamics and finds that Bi-Stride Multi-Scale Graph Neural Network and Transolver(++) are the most promising for airfoil and aircraft pressure prediction.
engineering_relevance: These models could reduce CFD cost in shape optimization, load analysis, and other design workflows that require many high-fidelity flow evaluations.
method: Tested on 2D airfoils of varying complexity and an industrial-scale 3D aircraft.
Assessed shock capture, scalability to large meshes, and performance under limited data.
evidence_signal: The study uses two aerodynamics experiments to compare surface-pressure prediction quality across complex geometries, large mesh sizes, and data-scarce settings.
watch_item: Performance is benchmark-specific, so deployment should account for geometry complexity, shock behavior, and mesh-scale limits before replacing CFD.
paper_title: Evaluation of State-of-the-Art Deep Learning Architectures for Aerodynamical Predictions
